content: The alternate drug pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Patients should avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, erythromycin lactobionate increases the QTc interval when combined with drugs like primaquine, erythromycin lactobionate, prochlorperazine, promethazine, and others. These combinations should be avoided or replaced with alternative drugs. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of quetiapine, quinidine, and ranolazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution or alternative therapies. It also increases the effects of repaglinide, repotrectinib, and resmetirom through various mechanisms, including P-glycoprotein inhibition and OATP1B1/3 transport inhibition. Co-administration with these drugs is not recommended. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, requiring avoidance or alternative therapy. Rifampin and rifapentine reduce the effects of erythromycin lactobionate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, and their use is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like tadalafil, temsirolimus, and tacrolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments or alternative therapies are recommended. It also increases the QTc interval when combined with drugs like sevoflurane, siponimod, and solifenacin, necessitating caution or avoidance. St. John’s Wort reduces the effects of erythromycin lactobionate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution or alternative therapy. Similarly, erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like sunitinib, tolvaptan, and topotecan through various mechanisms, including P-glycoprotein inhibition. Dose adjustments or alternative therapies are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of venetoclax and verapamil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with verapamil is contraindicated, while venetoclax requires dose reduction and close monitoring for toxicity. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of vilanterol and fluticasone by prolonging the QTc interval, necessitating caution. It also increases the effects of vilazodone and voriconazole through CYP3A4 metabolism, with voriconazole use contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the effects of live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like albuterol, alfuzosin, and amlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of cannabidiol and capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reductions are recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the effects of bactericidal agents like cefdinir, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised when combining these agents. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like ceritinib, cevimeline, and chlorpromazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like bortezomib, bosentan, and brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments or close monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants and long-acting injections by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored for signs of overmedication or withdrawal, and dose adjustments may be required. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of cabazitaxel and cabozantinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like atorvastatin and avanafil by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transport. Dose adjustments and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like azithromycin and aliskiren by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate reduces the effects of oral biotin and bortezomib by altering intestinal flora or affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like bromocriptine and budesonide by unknown mechanisms or P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like brexpiprazole and bromocriptine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism or unknown mechanisms. Dose adjustments and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like ceritinib and cevimeline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of drugs like chlorpromazine and ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
